subject: history_social
passage: Historians have long disagreed about the craft guilds that regulated trades in European towns from the twelfth century to the eighteenth. One tradition portrays them as guardians of quality: guild statutes set standards for materials and workmanship, required years of apprenticeship, and let inspectors seize shoddy goods, so that a buyer of Florentine cloth could trust what the name promised. A rival tradition sees the same rules as a monopoly in disguise, since limiting who could practice a trade also limited competition and kept prices high. Recent work has tended to dissolve the opposition rather than settle it. Whether a given guild protected consumers or exploited them, these scholars suggest, depended on how far the town's rulers could hold it accountable, which varied enormously from one city to the next.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It presents two competing interpretations of an institution and then explains why recent scholarship has endorsed the second.
choices.B: It presents two competing interpretations of an institution and then describes recent scholarship that treats the disagreement as depending on local circumstances.
choices.C: It traces the history of guilds from the twelfth century to the eighteenth and explains why they eventually disappeared.
choices.D: It describes how guilds enforced quality standards and then lists the trades in which those standards were strictest.

explanation.why: The text lays out two opposing views of guilds (guardians of quality versus monopoly in disguise). It then says recent scholarship has tried "to dissolve the opposition rather than settle it": which view fits depended on local accountability, "which varied enormously from one city to the next." So the structure is two interpretations, then a reframing that makes the answer depend on circumstances.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Recent work does not endorse the monopoly view; it dissolves the opposition "rather than settle it."
explanation.B: Correct. Two traditions are described, and recent work is said to make the answer depend on how accountable each guild was in its own town.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The dates only mark the period; the text says nothing about why guilds disappeared.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Enforcement is only part of the first interpretation, and the text does not rank trades by strictness.
